Homeschool Discovery Days - Whooo Ate That? – Owl Investigation
2550 G Ave
Ladora, IA
Map to Event
October 21, 2026
10:00 am · 11:00am
Discover the amazing world of owls! We’ll learn about the special adaptations that help owls hunt at night and put our own listening skills to the test with a fun owl hunting activity. Then, become a wildlife detective as we dissect real owl pellets! Participants will carefully uncover and identify tiny bones to discover what an owl has been eating and learn more about the important role owls play in the food chain. This hands-on program is designed for homeschool families of all ages. Come ready to listen, investigate, and discover the fascinating world of owls! Registration is required. Please sign up online at this link Homeschool-Discovery-Days-Whooo-Ate-That-Owl-Investigation sign-up . Only students need to register for this program. Please dress for the weather, as part of the program will take place outdoors.
Are you part of a larger private homeschool group? Contact us to learn about scheduling a separate Homeschool Discovery Day for your group!

Homeschool Discovery Days - Hidden Colors of Fall – Leaf Chromatograph
2550 G Ave
Ladora, IA
Map to Event
November 18, 2026
10:00 am · 11:00am
Have you ever wondered why leaves change color in the fall? Become a nature scientist as we uncover the hidden colors inside autumn leaves! Participants will use leaf chromatography to separate the different pigments found in leaves and discover that there may be more colors hiding inside a leaf than we can see. After our experiment, we’ll head outdoors to explore the trees around us. We’ll investigate fallen leaves, look for differences between tree species, and discover what happens to deciduous trees as they prepare for winter. Registration is required. Please sign up online at this link Homeschool-Discovery-Days-Hidden-Colors-of-Fall-Leaf-Chromatograph sign-up Only students need to register for this program. Please dress for the weather, as part of the program will take place outdoors.

About Iowa County
Iowa County, Iowa, was established in 1843. It is home to 7 communities, the Amana Colonies, and over 16,000 residents. The County is administered by a five-member Board of Supervisors who are elected for four-year terms. Other elected officials include the Attorney , Auditor , Recorder , Sheriff , and Treasurer .
